additional_info.subject: Issue Description
additional_info.body:
Actros e600; ignition could no longer be switched on, and the vehicle could not be put into "ready" mode. The vehicle had various active error codes, and it was discovered that the 24-volt system was discharged to approximately 4 volts. After replacing the 12-volt, the vehicle could be started again, and the errors could
be cleared; otherwise, no abnormalities were present. Subsequent clarifications with the manufacturer revealed that the problem exists with the Siemens charging station and is known (see Daimler Truck information GI54.10-N-085600 (I cannot upload pdf to the More app, if you need contact Alexander.mueller@siemens.com and i will provide you with the Daimler Trucks document). The costs are 1870.- CHF excl. VAT have been incurred for the
entire operation. Daimler Truck is not providing any warranty services for this case and refers to Siemens.
The vehicle functions without problems so far. Is this issue known? Are we cover these costs?

additional_info.subject: ID0438916-DC/Si-D/CH-[MP / S0 170004175] Charger discharged vehicle CRM:02919000211
additional_info.body:
Hi Alexander,
After a thorough investigation, I would like to clarify several important points regarding the charging process and vehicle interaction:
System Architecture and Control:
The vehicle's onboard systems, not the charging station, maintain complete control over the auxiliary battery management
The wake-up functionality is entirely managed by the vehicle's internal systems
The charging station does not have direct control over the vehicle's power management systems
Charging Session Management:
Our SiD implement a strict session management protocol where:
The charging session is automatically terminated when transitioning from PilotState C to B
No new session is initiated without specific prerequisites being met
The station requires all of the following conditions to even attempt a new session:
EcoG firmware version 1.4.11
Active OCPP backend connection
Specific OCPP configuration with TxStopPoint=PowerPathClosed
Technical Verification:
Our charging stations are designed to disengage completely from active communication once a charging session is properly terminated. The station cannot independently "wake up" the vehicle or force it to maintain an active state.
Given these technical facts, we can confirm that the charging station is not the root cause of the 12V battery discharge. The management of the auxiliary battery's charge state and the vehicle's wake-up functionality falls under the vehicle's internal power management system.
Please let me know your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco
